sn17.24:1.4: Also at [an2.133]() and [an4.176:4.2](). | Khujjuttarā was the most learned of the laywomen ([an1.260]()). | Veḷukaṇṭakī features as a meditator, reciter, and donor at [an6.37]() and [an7.53](). She is probably the same person as Uttarā Nanda’s mother who was the foremost laywoman jhana practitioner ([an1.262]()).
sn17.24:1.7: Also at [an2.131]() and [an4.176:2.2](). | Uppalavaṇṇā was the foremost nun in psychic powers ([an1.237]()), which kept her fearless when demolishing Māra ([sn5.5]()). Her verses are at [thig11.1](), and she was as a teacher of nuns ([thig13.5:27.3](), [pli-tv-kd20:8.1.1]()). A Vinaya story shows her gratitude to the Buddha ([pli-tv-bu-vb-np5:1.1.1]()). She was a survivor of sexual assault ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pj1:10.5.1]()). | Khemā was extolled as the foremost nun in wisdom ([an1.236]()); her verses are at [thig6.3](); and she teaches King Pasenadi in [sn44.1]().
